analysis.title: When Quality outruns Momentum
key_insights: Quality factor ETF (QUAL) is near record highs, but dispersion beneath the surface is unusually high. The focus shifts to Quality stocks that have lagged despite resilient earnings, cash generation and capital returns.

The Democratic sweep in the US midterms landed on a rotation already underway. Initial reaction was dispersion rather than broad risk aversion: solar and clean energy repriced most positively, banks and small caps opened higher, traditional energy and defence lagged, and semiconductors underperformed within Technology.

A less predictable policy backdrop, tighter fiscal constraints and wider sector dispersion could reinforce selectivity toward earnings visibility, balance-sheet strength and internally financed growth. The midterm result may reinforce the rotation rather than having started it.

The extreme style divergence (Momentum surging in H1 2026 while Quality fell) has largely closed. Pictet says the easy mean-reversion phase may be largely behind, and further Quality leadership needs earnings durability and capital efficiency.

QUAL has outperformed MTUM by about 12.6 percentage points over the past month and 7.9 points over three months, with near-identical year-to-date performance. The QUAL/MTUM ratio has reclaimed its 200-day moving average and is testing its prior downtrend, with 0.79 the immediate pivot and 0.83 the next major retracement level.

MTUM's profitable mega-cap AI exposure fell from 13.2% to 4.8% (Nvidia, Microsoft and Meta exited) while its AI infrastructure exposure rose from near zero to almost 39%. QUAL held close to 30% in profitable mega-cap AI and raised AI infrastructure exposure from 6.2% to 11.2% (Lam Research, Applied Materials, KLA).

Within AI, capital-efficient suppliers and physical infrastructure gained about 74% and 70% through September, and capacity owners rose 43%. In October capacity owners fell 24%, suppliers 21% and physical infrastructure 14%, versus 8% for monetisers and under 1% for the broader market. Pictet says this does not suggest AI demand has broken.

Price and earnings expectations have diverged. All 11 sampled stocks have positive 3M NTM EPS revisions and negative 3M price returns. Among seven AI infrastructure stocks, median EPS revisions were +26.7% against a median return of -27.5%.

In a preliminary analysis of about 300 US large caps, the highest ROIC quintile returned 14.2% over 1M versus -3.4% for the lowest, a 17.6pp spread. Pictet argues capital efficiency is becoming a bigger differentiator, and the next phase should reward companies that turn investment into durable returns.

QUAL is in an Elliott Wave sequence from the April 2025 low, consistent with a potential final wave 5. It consolidates below 228.13 resistance, above the 50-day MA at 223.26 and 200-day MA at 212.91. A break above 228.13 targets 235.45 and 239.95.
Breadth is lagging price: fewer than 70% of QUAL constituents are above their 200-day moving average, after breadth fell below 50% in the summer correction.

Pictet's contrarian screen on QUAL constituents requires PTS Quality Grade above 55, PTS Global Grade above 50 and PTS Relative Strength below 50, to find Quality without Momentum where fundamentals are intact.

tension_points.bull_case: AI demand and earnings expectations remain strong, with positive 3M NTM EPS revisions across all 11 sampled stocks and median +26.7% for seven AI infrastructure names.
tension_points.bear_case: The market is questioning whether growth can exceed expectations embedded in valuations, and capacity-exposed names fell 14% to 24% in October despite positive revisions.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A sustained move in the QUAL/MTUM ratio above 0.83 would signal continued Quality leadership over Momentum, and QUAL breaking above 228.13 would confirm the Quality advance.

theme_stances.key_argument: Quality has broken away from Momentum as the market shifts from capex exposure to capital efficiency, and the easy mean-reversion phase may be largely behind.
Exposure to rising AI spending may no longer be sufficient on its own, and the next phase should reward companies that turn investment into durable returns.
The opportunity is in Quality stocks where fundamentals are intact but relative price performance is weak.
theme_stances.evidence: The opportunity is in Quality laggards
